content: 1. Gemifloxacin has been discontinued in the United States. 2. For acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis caused by multidrug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae, Klebsiella pneumoniae, or Moraxella catarrhalis, the recommended dose is 320 mg orally once daily for 5 days. 3. For mild-to-moderate community-acquired pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae (including multidrug-resistant strains), Haemophilus influenzae, Haemophilus parainfluenzae, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Chlamydia pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis, or Mycoplasma pneumoniae, the recommended dose is 320 mg orally once daily for 7 days. 4. Gemifloxacin may also be effective against Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), Streptococcus pyogenes, Acinetobacter lwoffii, Klebsiella oxytoca, Legionella pneumophila, and Proteus vulgaris. However, its safety and efficacy for these indications have not been fully established. 5. Gemifloxacin and dronedarone both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together due to the increased risk of torsades de pointes, other serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. 6. Gemifloxacin and quinidine both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 7. Gemifloxacin and thioridazine both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 8. Co-administration of gemifloxacin with adagrasib should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug, as both agents prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes and other arrhythmias. If co-administration is unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended. 9. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the absorption of gemifloxacin in the gastrointestinal tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or separate dosing by at least 2 hours. 10. Aminolevulinic acid (oral) and gemifloxacin may increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Additionally, avoid administering other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid during the perioperative period. 11. Gemifloxacin increases the toxicity of aminolevulinic acid (topical) through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of photosensitizing drugs may enhance phototoxic reactions during photodynamic therapy with aminolevulinic acid. 12. Gemifloxacin and amiodarone both prolong the QTc interval.
